Testimony of Senator Bruce Bickford co-sponsoring
LD 114, An Act to Amend the Charter of the Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution Control Authority
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology
Good morning, Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and members of the Energy, Utilities and Technology Committee. My name is Bruce Bickford, and I represent Senate District 20, which includes Auburn, Durham, Poland, and New Gloucester. I am pleased to co-sponsor LD 114, An Act to Amend the Charter of the Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution Control Authority.
The Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution Control Authority (LAWPCA) is a quasi-municipal entity whose mission is to protect public health and the environment by treating the residential, commercial, and industrial wastewaters of our communities and returning clean water to the Androscoggin River.
On their 50th anniversary last year, LAWPCA decided that they wanted a name that focused on the end product of their treatment process, which is clean water. LD 114 would allow the entity to operate under the new name, Lewiston Auburn Clean Water Authority (LACWA).
Because of the way their charter is written, a name change requires legislative action. This change is purely administrative and will allow the Authority to update their business operations, including bank accounts and accounts payable/receivable.
I am happy to answer any questions, but Paula Drouin, Assistant General Manager of the Authority, is present today and is able to answer them.
Thank you for your consideration.

Testimony ofRep. Kristen Cloutier presenting
LD 114, An Act to Amend the Charter of the Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution
Control Authority Before the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology
Good morning, Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs and members of the Energy, Utilities and
Technology Committee. My name is Kristen Cloutier, and I represent House District 94, which includes part of my hometown of Lewiston. I am pleased to sponsor LD 114, An Act to Amend
the Charter of the Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution Control Authority.
The Lewiston-Auburn Water Pollution Control Authority (LAWPCA) is a quasi-municipal entity
managing the wastewater treatment system for Lewiston, Auburn and surrounding communities. They are the second-largest treatment plant in Maine.
On their 50th anniversary, LAWPCA decided that they wanted a name that better reflected their mission and values. LD 114 would allow the entity to operate under the name Lewiston Auburn
Clean Water Authority.
Because of the way their charter is written, this simple name change requires legislative action that
will provide the Authority with the ability to update their business operations, including bank
accounts and billing infonnation. The change is purely administrative, updating their name to more
accurately represent their current function while maintaining their existing operational
responsibilities.
I am happy to answer any questions, but Paula Drouin, Assistant General Manager of the Authority, and slated to speak after me, may be better suited to address them.
Thank you for your consideration.

District 94: Part of Lewiston
